_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for El Salvador covering Joya de Cerén ('Pompeii of the Americas'), Ilopango eruption 431 CE, Pipil/Nahua migration, Maya influences, Alvarado conquest, cacao/indigo colonial economy, independence 1821, coffee oligarchy ('14 families'), 1932 La Matanza massacre (~30,000 indigenous killed, Farabundo Martí), civil war 1980-92 (~75,000 dead, death squads, Oscar Romero assassination), MS-13/Barrio 18 gangs, and Bukele's authoritarian anti-gang crackdown.

country_profile.currency: United States dollar (USD, since 2001); Bitcoin (legal tender since 2021, world first)

religion.note: Rapidly evangelicalizing (approaching parity with Catholicism); Archbishop Oscar Romero (assassinated 1980, canonized 2018); liberation theology crucible; Jesuit martyrs of UCA (6 killed 1989); charismatic Protestantism strong in poor communities

ethnic_groups.name: Mestizo
ethnic_groups.notes: Mixed Indigenous-European; dominant identity; indigenous heritage largely erased after 1932 La Matanza (Indigenous stopped wearing traditional dress, speaking Nawat for survival); culturally homogeneous

ethnic_groups.name: White
ethnic_groups.notes: Spanish descent; '14 families' elite (oligarchs who controlled coffee economy); Palestinians/Lebanese (powerful: e.g., Bukele family, Saca, Handal); some German, French

ethnic_groups.name: Indigenous
ethnic_groups.notes: Pipil/Nahua (Nawat speakers, ~200-500 fluent), Lenca, Kakawira (Cacaopera); effectively made invisible by 1932 Matanza; Nawat revival efforts; undercount likely

ethnic_groups.name: Afro-Salvadoran
ethnic_groups.notes: Historically erased; small; recognition recent; colonial-era slavery existed but smaller than Caribbean

independence.from: Spain (as part of Central American independence)

country_profile.notes_unique: Smallest and most densely populated mainland Americas country; Joya de Cerén (UNESCO, 'Pompeii of the Americas', preserved by volcanic ash ~600 CE); La Matanza 1932 (~30,000 indigenous killed, erased indigenous identity); civil war 1980-92 (FMLN vs. government, US-backed death squads, Archbishop Romero assassinated at altar 1980, UCA Jesuits killed 1989); MS-13 and Barrio 18 gangs (deported from LA, terrorized country); Bukele (most popular yet most authoritarian modern leader, state of exception since 2022, ~70,000 arrested); Bitcoin legal tender 2021 (first country); pupusas; 'El Pulgarcito de América' (The Tom Thumb)

governance_indices.notes: Nayib Bukele's mass incarceration strategy reduced homicides dramatically

economy_extended.notes: Bitcoin adopted as legal tender in 2021

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Nayib Bukele
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Nuevas Ideas party; Palestinian descent; social media savvy; anti-gang state of exception (2022-present, ~70,000 arrested, due process concerns); Bitcoin adoption; mega-prison (CECOT); 90%+ approval; constitutional concerns (re-elected 2024 despite one-term limit); authoritarian populism model

former_leaders.name: Salvador Sánchez Cerén
former_leaders.notes: FMLN; former guerrilla commander; stagnation; gang violence; migration crisis

former_leaders.name: Mauricio Funes
former_leaders.notes: FMLN; first left-wing president; journalist; corruption (fled to Nicaragua, asylum); gang truce 2012-14 (controversial)

former_leaders.name: Antonio 'Tony' Saca
former_leaders.notes: ARENA; Palestinian descent; convicted of embezzling $300M (sentenced 10 years)

former_leaders.name: Francisco Flores
former_leaders.notes: ARENA; dollarization 2001; died awaiting corruption trial

former_leaders.name: Alfredo Cristiani
former_leaders.notes: ARENA; signed Chapultepec Peace Accords 1992 (ended civil war); coffee oligarch; UCA massacre occurred under his watch

former_leaders.name: José Napoleón Duarte
former_leaders.notes: PDC; Christian Democrat; civil war president; US-backed; moderate; earthquake 1986; corruption allegations; died of cancer

former_leaders.name: Military Junta/Presidents
former_leaders.notes: Series of military rulers; Maximiliano Hernández Martínez (La Matanza 1932); succession of colonels/generals; ORDEN paramilitaries; triggered civil war
